title: cicd.yaml
description: Developer-facing pipeline configuration. This is the only file app teams edit to control their CI/CD pipelines - it never contains Tekton, YAML pipeline steps, or infrastructure details. Validated fail-fast by the validate-cicd-config Task before any other pipeline step runs.

agent.description: Named build agent image from the platform catalog. Not a raw image reference - keeps step code portable and centrally patchable. Still required even when `script` is omitted, since unit tests always run inside this image regardless of build strategy.

script.description: Build script the platform runs inside the agent image before packaging. Must be bash. Omit entirely for teams doing the whole build inside a multi-stage Dockerfile - the separate build-source stage is skipped and kaniko builds `dockerfile` directly. No default: presence/absence is the switch, so it can't silently mean 'skip' via an unrelated typo.

enabled.description: Persistent dependency-download cache for build-source (npm's package cache / Maven's local repository, not node_modules/target itself - see docs/cicd-yaml-reference.md). No `type` field: derived from `agent`'s prefix (nodejs-* -> npm, openjdk-* -> maven), not a second, redundantly-declarable field. Keyed by a hash of the relevant lockfile (package-lock.json/pom.xml) so a dependency change invalidates the cache automatically. A no-op (logged, not an error) for agents without cache support yet (python-*/go-1.22). Teams with no build.script (whole build inside a multi-stage Dockerfile) get layer caching for free from kaniko instead.

size.description: T-shirt size for this app's own cache PVC (small=1Gi, medium=2.5Gi, large=5Gi, xlarge=8Gi - same dictionary as the old cd-pipelines-user Helm chart's buildSpec.cacheSize). One PVC per app, specifically so this can vary per app. Chosen at onboarding time, not resizable live afterward - kind-observe's default storage class has allowVolumeExpansion: false, so changing this later means recreating the PVC (and losing its cached content), not a live resize.

T-shirt size for the ephemeral `source` workspace every stage's PipelineRun gets (small=2Gi, medium=5Gi, large=10Gi, xlarge=20Gi). This is the checked-out git repo plus build.script's own output plus kaniko's build context - distinct from build.cache (a separate, persistent, per-app dependency-download cache). Exists because a large build can genuinely fill this workspace's disk ('no space left on device'), not because of anything cache-related. Not per-stage: one size applies to every stage's source workspace for this app (build/test/deploy/release all declare the same `source` workspace shape), since build is normally the only stage large enough to need this, and a single per-app knob is simpler than one per stage. Not resizable live - each PipelineRun's workspace is a fresh, ephemeral volumeClaimTemplate-backed PVC (unlike build.cache's persistent one), so a size change just takes effect on the next run, nothing to migrate.

name.description: Name of the TestWorkflow to run (platform/<name>.yaml in this repo).

oneOf.description: Same-cluster upper env (today's default/only behavior) - RBAC is provisioned into a same-cluster namespace exactly like a lowerEnvironments entry.

name.description: The env name release steps refer to via their own env: field, e.g. "staging".

cluster.description: Name of an entry in the control-plane chart's clusters: registry (see docs/multi-cluster.md) - the physical cluster this env's ArgoCD Application actually lives on. Setting this means no same-cluster RBAC is provisioned for this env (there's no local namespace for it) and release promotions for it go through the GitOps app-of-apps delivery path instead of a direct in-cluster apply.

upperEnvironments.description: Which upper (release-stage) environments this app has, and optionally which cluster each one lives on. A release step's env: must name one of these; if that entry is the object form, the step's own optional cluster: (if set) must agree with it. See docs/multi-cluster.md.

strategy.description: deployment = native k8s Deployment rollout; rollout = Argo Rollouts (canary/blue-green). Schema-validated and reserved for future use, but rollout has NO effect yet - every deploy is a plain Deployment `set image` regardless of this value. Kept in the schema now, same as pipelines[].steps[].cluster, so today's cicd.yaml files don't need a breaking change once Argo Rollouts support lands.

promotionOrder.description: Optional, full ordered list of every env (lower AND upper) a release should pass through, e.g. [dev, test, rel, staging, pre-prod, prod]. Not enforced by platform-cicd's own automation - no Task or Trigger reads this today, and it does not need to equal what any single pipeline's own deploy/release steps cover. It exists as an explicit, authoritative declaration of the full intended promotion sequence for consumers that need it (Backstage's Glidepath plugin: it otherwise has to infer env order by finding whichever pipeline has the most deploy/release steps, which silently breaks once a pipeline legitimately covers only part of the sequence - e.g. build/test/deploy-to-dev only, leaving every later stage to a manual promotion path). Every entry should name an env declared in this app's own lowerEnvironments or upperEnvironments; a consumer encountering an unrecognized entry should treat the whole list as unusable and fall back to its own inference rather than trust a partial/stale list. Not cross-validated against lowerEnvironments/upperEnvironments by validate-cicd-config today.

ttl.description: How long an ephemeral environment lives after its last successful deploy before automatic teardown.

governance.description: Quality/security gates. sast/imageScan/policyCheck/sbom are real, live-enforcing gates (Semgrep/Trivy/gitsign+Fulcio/cosign SBOM attestation respectively - see docs/governance-stubs.md for exactly what each one verifies), not stubs.

policyCheck.description: Controls only the build-time shift-left copy of this scan, if one exists. The release-gate commit-signature check (catalog/tasks/verify-commit-signature.yaml) runs unconditionally on every release PR regardless of this flag - release gates are enforced, not app-configurable. Populate allowedCommitSigners below either way.

allowedCommitSigners.description: Plain email addresses gitsign's --certificate-identity-regexp is built from at verify time (see catalog/tasks/verify-commit-signature.yaml). Always consulted by the release-gate commit-signature check regardless of policyCheck's value - an app that leaves this empty fails that check on every release. One entry per allowed human signer; no regex syntax needed here.

scanResults.description: Shift-left notifications from sast-scan/image-scan the moment each real scan produces a result, separate from the general build/test/deploy/release pass-fail notification above (which stays on whenever slack.enabled is true). Only takes effect when slack.enabled is also true. Defaults on (matching the pipeline's own default real-scan behavior), but an app that finds these too frequent/verbose can turn just this off without losing the general per-stage notifications.

enabled.description: Sends the same build/test/deploy/release pass-fail notification as notifications.slack into Backstage's own Notifications plugin (broadcast to every Backstage user, viewable in Tower's Notifications tab), instead of/in addition to Slack. Independent toggle - either target can be on, off, or both. Requires the cluster's glidepath-catalog chart to have backstageBaseUrl and a glidepath-backstage-notify token secret configured (see docs/admin/notifications.md); a cluster without that setup skips silently.

secrets.description: Optional. Each entry pulls one key out of this Application's own backend secret store (assumed provisioned alongside the Application itself - see docs/app-secrets.md - NOT something platform-cicd creates) and lands it as a key in this Application's app-secrets Kubernetes Secret, synced by a real ExternalSecret. Open-ended by design: a brand-new secret purpose (SAST creds, a DB password, anything else a future Task needs) is a new list entry here, not a schema/template change - whatever Task consumes it just needs to know which `name` to look for. Empty by default: the SecretStore/ExternalSecret are only rendered at all when this list is non-empty, so an Application that doesn't use this feature gets no dangling resources pointed at a secrets namespace that may not exist for it.

name.description: Logical name. Becomes the key inside the app-secrets Kubernetes Secret this renders - a consuming Task mounts app-secrets and reads this exact filename. Also the default for `key` below, so the common case (the name you want to use here already matches the name it has in your backend store) needs only this one field.

key.description: Key name as it actually exists in the app's own backend secret store object. Defaults to `name` when omitted - only set this when the backend key is named differently than you want it exposed as.

pipelines.description: Optional named pipeline flows. Each flow can define a root trigger and an ordered list of stages, allowing app teams to describe build -> test -> deploy -> release sequences without writing Tekton YAML directly. The legacy list form used by earlier config files is also accepted and normalized by the chart.

source.description: Preferred explicit shape: git triggers evaluate branch/path filters; event triggers use the broker CDEvents path and the event field.

event.description: Explicit event identifier for the root trigger. For git sources this is the Git event kind; for event sources it is the CDEvents event type. No release.created - confirmed live that Pipelines-as-Code has no support for GitHub 'release' webhooks at all (any version): a real delivery came back '{"status":200,"message":"skipping non supported event"}', filtered out before PaC's own annotation matching ever runs, so no Trigger config could ever make this fire. Use 'tag' instead - publishing a GitHub Release also creates the underlying tag, which fires a real, working push event.

type.description: Legacy shorthand for the git-trigger form. Newer configs should use source+event.

tagPattern.description: Regex the pushed tag's name must match, required when event is 'tag' (e.g. 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'). See deliver-onboarding-files.yaml's generate_flow_file.

labels.description: Only meaningful when event is 'pull_request'. If set, the flow only fires for a PR carrying ALL of these GitHub labels (same all-must-match semantics as ArgoCD's own pullRequest generator labels: field, for consistency between the build trigger and the ephemeral-environment deploy trigger that reads the same PR). Omit for no label filter (fires on every PR touching this branch). See deliver-onboarding-files.yaml's generate_flow_file.

testName.description: Only meaningful on a test step. Overrides the top-level test.name for this specific step - needed when a flow has more than one test step (they'd otherwise be indistinguishable). Falls back to test.name when omitted; one of the two must resolve to a value, since a TestWorkflow run always needs a name. Not called `name` - that field below is the deploy/release target name, a different concept.

gitopsRepo.description: Only meaningful (and required) on a gitops-image-bump step: the gitops repo (by name, e.g. 'gitops-cluster-kind-man') to open the image-bump PR against. Unlike release's gitops-<app-name> convention, this stage is for a hand-deployed singleton/cluster-config component whose manifests don't live in a per-app gitops repo, so the target repo must be named explicitly. Requires an extra Repository CR granting this app's CI namespace write access - see platformIdentity.extraGitopsRepos in the tenant identity.yaml (not this repo's cicd.yaml, since it's a trust/authorization grant the app owner doesn't self-serve).

manifestPath.description: Only meaningful (and required) on a gitops-image-bump step: path within gitopsRepo to a plain Kubernetes manifest (not airframe-application Helm values.yaml) whose first container's image field gets patched, e.g. '60-backstage/backstage/deployment.yaml'.
